what_its_for: Loncastuximab tesirine is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of blood cancer called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or other related B-cell lymphomas that have come back or did not respond to at least two previous treatments. It works by attaching to cancer cells and delivering a powerful substance that destroys them.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a healthcare provider through an IV (intravenous) infusion, which means it goes directly into your vein. You will receive this infusion at a clinic or infusion center. Before each dose, you will be given a steroid medicine (dexamethasone) to help reduce the risk of a serious side effect called fluid buildup. You do not take this medicine at home.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your body size (height and weight). It is usually given once every 3 weeks (called a treatment cycle). You will receive it for the first two cycles, and then your doctor may adjust how often you get it based on how your body responds. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing schedule.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider at a clinic, it is unlikely you will miss a dose. However, if you miss or need to reschedule your appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to set up a new time. Do not try to double up on doses.
storage: This medicine is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals at the clinic. You do not need to store it at home. If you are given any related medicines to take at home (like steroids), store them at room temperature away from heat, moisture, and light, and keep them out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while on this treatment, as it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 10 months after your last dose (for women) or 7 months (for men). Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 3 months after your last dose. Avoid people who are sick with infections, as this medicine can weaken your immune system. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience any of the following: sudden or unusual weight gain or swelling (especially in your belly, arms, legs, or face), difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher or signs of infection (chills, cough, painful urination), unusual bruising or bleeding, skin reactions such as rash, blistering, peeling, or open sores, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, severe tiredness, dark urine or yellowing of your skin or eyes. These could be signs of serious side effects that need immediate attention.
when_it_works: Every patient is different. Some people may start to see improvement after a few treatment cycles, but it may take several weeks or months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular tests and scans. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor, even if you do not feel different right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby and should not be used during pregnancy. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control. Do not breastfeed while on this medicine. Older Adults: Older patients can receive this medicine but may need extra monitoring for side effects. Liver or Kidney Problems: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney problems, as this may affect how the medicine works in your body and your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old.
